headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 5 studies yielded an effect size of 0.97 (95% CI: 0.66–1.41), indicating no statistically significant association between Vitamin C and renal cell carcinoma. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 81.10%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.

studies.Population: Male Finnish smokers aged 50-69 years in the ATBC Study cohort
studies.comparison_type: Highest versus lowest quartile of vitamin C intake

sample_size.excerpt: At baseline, 27,062 male Finnish smokers aged 50-69 years completed a 276-item dietary questionnaire that included questions on frequency of consumption and portion size. During up to 19 years of follow-up, 255 men developed RCC.
sample_size.location: abstract

cases.excerpt: During up to 19 years of follow-up, 255 men developed RCC.

effect_size.excerpt: Despite a large range in intake, no association was observed between fruit, vegetables or antioxidant nutrients and RCC risk. For example, multivariate RRs and 95% CIs for the highest versus the lowest quartile of intake were 0.79 (0.55-1.14), 1.23 (0.85-1.79), 1.09 (0.74-1.60), 0.83 (0.57-1.21), 1.09 (0.73-1.64) and 0.99 (0.67-1.46) for fruit, vegetables, total carotenoids, total flavonoids, total vitamin E and vitamin C, respectively (all p values for trend > 0.05).

sample_size.excerpt: In the current analysis, we included all participants in the clinical trials and the observational study except for women who enrolled in the Dietary Modification clinical trial (n = 48,835) who had a history of any cancer other than nonmelanoma skin cancers at study entry 7 , 10 , 12 or who had implausible energy intakes (<600 or >5000 kcal daily) at baseline (n = 4067). This resulted in an inclusive total of 96,196 women in our analytic cohort.

studies.Population: Population-based US Kidney Cancer Study participants in Detroit and Chicago
studies.comparison_type: lowest vs highest quartile (<=144 vs >666 mg/day)

sample_size.excerpt: 1142 EA and AA RCC cases and 1154 frequency‐matched controls were enrolled in a population‐based case‐control study between 2002 and 2007.
sample_size.location: Methods, Study population, paragraph 2; total_n derived from reported group counts 1142 + 1154 = 2296

cases.excerpt: Sociodemographic and baseline health characteristics and nutrient intake levels of 1142 cases and 1154 controls in the eligible study population are presented by race in Table 1 . Compared to controls, cases were more likely to report a lower education level, smoke, have a higher BMI and family history of RCC, and diagnosed with hypertension.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Associations between individual micronutrients and RCC risk were assessed using unconditional logistic regression models to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) from adjusted models. These analyses were weighted using a jackknife replication method (Jackknife 2).

comparison.excerpt: the three lower quartiles were each compared to the highest quartile

design.excerpt: The US Kidney Cancer Study is a population‐based case‐control study designed to examine racial disparities between AA and EA in RCC risk.

continent.excerpt: The study was conducted in the metropolitan areas of Detroit (Wayne, Oakland, and Macomb counties), Michigan and Chicago (Cook County), Illinois.

ethnicity.excerpt: Eligible cases were EA and AA men and women between the ages of 20 and 79 years with newly diagnosed RCC.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: The DHQ was interviewer‐administered and queried frequency of intake for foods, beverages, multivitamin, vitamin C, and vitamin E supplements, for a total of 80 line items.

gender.excerpt: Eligible cases were EA and AA men and women between the ages of 20 and 79 years with newly diagnosed RCC.

smoking_status.excerpt: Adjusted models included variables for: region (Detroit, Chicago), sex (male, female), race (White, African American), age (20‐44, 45‐54, 55‐64, 65‐74, 75+), education (<12 years, high school graduate, some college, 4+ years of college), smoking history (never, occasional/unknown, former, current), BMI (<25, 25‐30, 30‐<35, 35+_kg/m 2 ), RCC family history (none with cancer, unknown if diagnosed with cancer, diagnosed with other type of cancer, diagnosed with kidney cancer), and TDCI (continuous variable).
